details: The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, rose faster than expected in May 2026. This hotter inflation data dampened market expectations for near-term interest rate cuts, leading to a decline in both US stocks and Bitcoin. Bitcoin's price reportedly fell to around $58,000, its lowest level since September 2024.
title: US PCE Inflation Rises, Dims Fed Rate Cut Hopes, Bitcoin Falls to 2026 Low

details: China is actively expanding its yuan-based cross-border payment network (CIPS) and promoting its digital yuan (mBridge), which is now handling billions in transactions and has added 26 new banks. This initiative is seen as weakening the global reach of US sanctions and dollar dominance, potentially enabling countries to bypass the US-centered financial order. This development also heightens regulatory scrutiny on cryptocurrencies, as they are increasingly cited as channels for circumventing sanctions.
title: China Bolsters Yuan Payments, Raising Concerns over US Sanctions Evasion via Crypto

details: The European Union has announced its 21st package of sanctions against Russia in response to the ongoing war in Ukraine. This latest round of measures includes new restrictions specifically targeting financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms, aiming to further pressure the Russian economy and its ability to fund the conflict.
title: EU's 21st Sanctions Package Against Russia Targets Crypto Platforms

details: A United Nations agency has temporarily suspended ship evacuations through the crucial Strait of Hormuz after a vessel was reportedly struck. Simultaneously, Iran has rejected a UN-backed proposal aimed at freeing ships currently trapped in the strait. These events signal escalating tensions and instability in the vital oil shipping route, which can lead to increased energy prices and a risk-off sentiment in global financial markets.
title: UN Agency Halts Hormuz Evacuations After Ship Struck, Iran Rejects Plan

details: A Wall Street Journal report, based on blockchain data, indicates that Iranian entities have transacted over $3.84 billion in cryptocurrency through the Seychelles-based exchange CoinEx since 2019. This activity has enabled Iran's crypto ecosystem to connect with global markets despite extensive US sanctions, highlighting the ongoing challenges in enforcing such restrictions within blockchain-based financial systems and potentially prompting further regulatory action against crypto platforms globally.
sourceName: Iran International (citing The Wall Street Journal)
title: Report: Iran Uses CoinEx Crypto Exchange to Circumvent US Sanctions
